candidate_profile.description: The candidate notices that the issue may be on the distribution side and that geography matters, but the diagnosis is incomplete and the final recommendation is still tentative and underdeveloped.
behaviour_rules: Recognize that sales growth alone does not explain falling profits, but do not frame the problem very sharply.
Ask some relevant questions on cost trends and channels, but not in a cleanly prioritized way.
Notice that distribution costs have risen, but do not fully connect them to open-state economics.
Acknowledge that open and regulated states are different, but explain the cost implications only partially.
Spend some unnecessary time checking product mix or price before ruling them out.
Be slow to conclude that the sales mix is shifting toward less profitable open states.
Give a directionally reasonable recommendation, but without much specificity on state-level profitability or distribution actions.

expected_issues: Only partially explains why open states are less profitable to serve.
Does not sharply rule out product mix and pricing as root causes.
Underdevelops the significance of shrinking regulated-state volume.
Recommendation is too broad and not tightly tied to channel economics.
expected_feedback_points: Prioritize the channel and distribution question earlier.
Explain more clearly why open states require more expensive trade support and more frequent deliveries.
State explicitly that the mix shift toward open states is hurting overall profitability.
Recommend profitability analysis by state type and more targeted actions in the higher-cost channel.
